stem: If \(3 \le a \le 7\) and \(-4 \le b \le 2\), what is the greatest possible value of \(a - b\)?
solution: To make \(a - b\) as great as possible, make \(a\) as great as possible and \(b\) as small as possible.
The greatest \(a\) is 7 and the least \(b\) is \(-4\).
So the greatest value of \(a - b\) is \(7 - (-4) = 11\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This uses the greatest value of \(b\), 2, but subtracting a greater number makes the difference smaller: \(7 - 2 = 5\).
explanation.B: Correct. The greatest value of \(a\) minus the least value of \(b\) gives \(7 - (-4) = 11\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This uses the least value of \(a\), 3: \(3 - (-4) = 7\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This computes \(7 + 2\), adding the greatest value of \(b\) instead of subtracting the least value.

verify:
choices = {o: choices[n] for o, n in {'A': 'A', 'D': 'B', 'B': 'C', 'C': 'D'}.items()}; answer = {'A': 'A', 'B': 'D', 'C': 'B', 'D': 'C'}[answer]  # shuffled: original letters
corners = [(p, q) for p in (3, 7) for q in (-4, 2)]
best = max(p - q for p, q in corners)
assert best == 11 and value(choices[answer]) == best
assert all(value(choices[k]) != best for k in choices if k != answer)
